proposal: The Mandate says the Secretary of State should revoke most outstanding Circular 175 (C-175) authorities that earlier administrations granted to other agencies, coordinating the revocations with the White House for logistical reasons. It criticizes the prior administration for delegating State's diplomatic capacity to agencies such as DHS, and the chapter elsewhere treats DHS as keeping or regaining a role in security agreements.
remaining: Any State review or revocation of outstanding C-175 delegations to non-State agencies.

status_summary: No State Department action revoking or narrowing C-175 delegations to other agencies was found. DHS has continued to be a party to international arrangements: its Federal Register notices publish asylum cooperative agreements with Honduras (signed 2025-03-10, with an amendment by notes exchanged 2025-06-25) and a memorandum with Paraguay (signed 2025-08-14). Those notices do not state the legal authority under which they were negotiated, so they do not show whether C-175 authority was revoked, retained or newly granted. The immigration agreements themselves are covered in c05-03.

timeline.event: A DHS, State and Paraguayan agency memorandum on asylum cooperation was signed at Washington, later published by DHS in the Federal Register; the notice does not state the authority basis.

title: Revoke most Circular 175 negotiating authorities held by other agencies
uncertainties: Searches for Circular 175 revocations, State Foreign Affairs Manual changes and DHS delegations found no public record either way. The two DHS notices read were short and their agreement text appears as images, so the signatories and authority basis could not be confirmed. Whether the Paraguay arrangement is a 2025-08-14 signature, as the notice states, was taken from the notice alone. Executive Order 14159 sections 12 and 13 direct DHS and State to use international agreements and talks on removals but do not mention C-175.
